# AUDIT 0002 - the three structural gaps between 13 asks and 23/23

Audit/0001 built all thirteen ask functions and landed both provider
reads, and still the 23-contact cohort cannot be cleared across the 23
rules (529 cells): twenty-three contacts times twenty-three rules, and the
instrument cannot print PASS for three of those rules no matter what the
data says, because the inputs those PASSes need are structurally absent.
This audit names the three gaps, prices the smallest change for each as a
proposal with its diff, UNAPPLIED, classifies each as instrument or
safety, and answers the honest question: with the 13 asks, the 4 hold-rule
asks and the 1 health reader all built, is 23/23 reachable, and when.

## The two SHAs every anchor is cited against

The lane branch base is `67dbeccc7d7a14627393cdb0f3c7e72752666355` (its tree is the audit/0001 state this audit
measured the instrument at). The canary lineage tip is `1ba54cdda541adee1a97e0401f0b3f678e1bbb3d` (tree `9138d4c920303195a2beb704d9ce47ddd73127c2`),
which is where the instrument, the bounce recorder's writer side, and
`suppression.decide` all coexist - every composed verification tree below
is that tip's tree plus one gap's proposal, extracted with `git cat-file`
because `ls-tree` and `archive` return empty in this environment.
`src/preflight.py` is byte-identical at both SHAs (blob `a3877f8b78e9b93616ff65a2b30f7c9aa77e8527`, 100833 B), so
every preflight line number below is true at either.

Every line number below was re-derived by searching the blob text at the
cited SHA. None was inherited from an earlier document.


## 1. Gap 1 - the recorder's failure line has one writer and no reader

### 1.1 The finding, re-derived

`scripts/bison_watch_loop.py`:601 (at the canary SHA) writes the one line
that says the bounce recorder failed:

    emit(f"BOUNCE-RECORD-FAILED {provider_id}: {type(exc).__name__}")

and nothing under `src/` reads it. That was pinned by test in audit/0001
(`test_the_estate_search_finds_the_writer_and_no_reader`) and re-measured
for this audit: exactly one occurrence in `src/`, `scripts/` and `tests/`
once the searching file itself is set aside - the writer - and zero under
`src/`, where any gate would live.

The consequence is structural, not incidental. `_ask_bounce_history`
(`src/preflight.py`:730) answers EXCLUDED when the record holds a bounce
event, and `Undecided` - which evaluates to UNKNOWN - when it holds none.
A contact with no recorded bounce is therefore UNKNOWN forever, because
"no bounce recorded" is ambiguous between "never bounced" and "the
recorder is broken and recorded nothing". The 14th instrument piece the
brief names is the one that disambiguates: a health reader for the
recorder. Without it, `bounce_history` can EXCLUDE and can refuse, and
can never PASS - so 23/23 is unreachable.


### 1.2 The smallest change, UNAPPLIED

Two edits and one test file, all against the canary SHA's blobs:

- `src/leadobserve.py`: `RECORDER_FAILED_KIND`, a `HEALTH_WINDOW_SECONDS`
  of two bison poll intervals, three states, and
  `recorder_health(now=None, window=...)` reading the heartbeat and the
  failure lines through the REAL sink readers (`watchsink.heartbeats`,
  `watchsink.events`) - no second file format, no second reader of the
  watcher's files.
- `src/preflight.py`: the `_ask_bounce_history` tail gates its PASS on
  HEALTHY and nothing else. One condition, and the rest of the ask is
  untouched.
- the tests: the two audit/0001 pins (zero readers of the failure line;
  zero production callers of `watchsink.events`) are re-pinned to EXACTLY
  ONE reader with the same shape of teeth, and six new tests run the
  reader through `watchsink.beat` and `watchsink.record` - the same
  writers the watcher uses - so the proof is about the reader, not about
  a file shape the test invented.

```diff
diff --git a/_0002_scratch/g1_leadobserve_orig.py b/_0002_scratch/g1_leadobserve_new.py
index d812614f1..f9fd7cc2c 100644
--- a/_0002_scratch/g1_leadobserve_orig.py
+++ b/_0002_scratch/g1_leadobserve_new.py
@@ -792,6 +792,113 @@ def record_bounces(campaign_id, queue=None, recs=None, live=False,
         rows=[row for row in rows if row["state"] == BOUNCED])
 
 
+#: The word the watcher's recorder-failure line begins with. `watchsink.record`
+#: derives an event's `kind` from the FIRST WORD of the line, so this is the
+#: token the sink already indexes that failure under - the reader below
+#: matches the kind, never the whole line. Until this reader existed the token
+#: was pinned to ZERO occurrences under `src/` by TASK-0220's search, which is
+#: how "nobody reads this failure" stayed a measurement; the pin now asserts
+#: exactly ONE occurrence - this one - and the test that owns it was updated
+#: in the same change.
+RECORDER_FAILED_KIND = "BOUNCE-RECORD-FAILED"
+
+#: The freshness window, from the supervisor's own arithmetic rather than a
+#: new number: STALE_BEAT_MULTIPLE (2, `src/supervisor.py` STALE_BEAT_MULTIPLE)
+#: x the 180-second interval the supervisor launches every bison watcher with
+#: (its `bison_campaign_id` registration). A recorder that is failing emits
+#: the failure kind on EVERY poll, so two missed intervals is proof that
+#: either it is not failing or the loop itself is gone - and the heartbeat
+#: halves decide which.
+HEALTH_WINDOW_SECONDS = 2 * 180
+
+#: Only HEALTHY licenses anything. The other two are both "do not clear".
+RECORDER_HEALTHY = "healthy"
+RECORDER_FAILING = "failing"
+RECORDER_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
+
+
+def recorder_health(now=None, window=HEALTH_WINDOW_SECONDS):
+    """(state, why). Is the bounce recorder working? READ ONLY.
+
+    THE 14TH PIECE, named by WHAT_WOULD_ANSWER["bounce_recorder"]: a reader
+    that reaches a verdict from the recorder's own health, which until this
+    function existed had ONE writer (`scripts/bison_watch_loop.py`'s
+    `_bounce_recorder`) and ZERO readers, so an empty `events` list could not
+    be told apart from a recorder failing for an unbounded time while the
+    watcher kept beating.
+
+    What it reads - the recorder's own two sinks, nothing else, no provider
+    call, no queue write:
+
+    * `work/heartbeat/bison-<id>.json`, rewritten by `watchsink.beat` on
+      every poll of every watched campaign;
+    * `work/watch-events/bison-<id>.jsonl`, append-only, the only place the
+      recorder's failure line lands.
+
+    HEALTHY   at least one bison heartbeat exists, every one present is
+              fresh inside `window`, and no event of the failure kind is
+              recorded inside `window` (a torn line whose fragment carries
+              the kind counts as one - undated is not old).
+    FAILING   an event of the failure kind inside `window`, or a heartbeat
+              that exists and cannot be read.
+    UNKNOWN   no bison heartbeat at all - the watcher is not running, which
+              is TASK-0220's own boundary, and NOT RUNNING IS NOT HEALTHY -
+              or a heartbeat gone stale inside the window.
+
+    UNHEALTHY MUST NOT READ AS CLEAN, and here is the mechanism rather than
+    the hope: the two non-HEALTHY states are distinct values with their own
+    why-sentence, and the only caller that licenses anything from them
+    (preflight's `_ask_bounce_history`) licenses a PASS on HEALTHY alone, so
+    FAILING and UNKNOWN both leave the cell UNKNOWN. There is no input to
+    this function that turns a failure into a healthy verdict: the failure
+    kind inside the window FAILS the read whatever the heartbeats say,
+    because a beating loop and a failing recorder are the same pair of files
+    (TASK-0220's C2 measured exactly that).
+    """
+    import time
+
+    from . import watchsink
+
+    now = time.time() if now is None else now
+    beats = [b for b in watchsink.heartbeats()
+             if str(b.get("source") or "").split(":", 1)[0] == "bison"]
+    if not beats:
+        return RECORDER_UNKNOWN, (
+            "no bison watcher heartbeat exists at all, so the recorder is "
+            "not running - not running is not the same as recording nothing")
+    problems = []
+    for beat in beats:
+        if beat.get("unreadable") or beat.get("epoch") is None:
+            problems.append("heartbeat %s cannot be read" % beat.get("watcher"))
+    stale = {row.get("watcher") for row in watchsink.stale(window, now=now)}
+    for beat in beats:
+        if beat.get("watcher") in stale:
+            problems.append("heartbeat %s is stale beyond %ss"
+                            % (beat.get("watcher"), window))
+    if problems:
+        return RECORDER_UNKNOWN, "; ".join(problems)
+
+    # The failure kind inside the window. `since` is compared as a string,
+    # exact for the `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` watchsink writes; a row with no `at`
+    # (a torn line) is kept rather than filtered, because undated is not old.
+    since = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(now - window))
+    failures = [row for row in watchsink.events(source="bison")
+                if (row.get("kind") == RECORDER_FAILED_KIND
+                    or (row.get("torn")
+                        and RECORDER_FAILED_KIND in (row.get("line") or "")))
+                and (row.get("at") is None
+                     or str(row.get("at")) >= since)]
+    if failures:
+        return RECORDER_FAILING, (
+            "%d recorder failure line(s) inside %ss, newest %s"
+            % (len(failures), window,
+               max(str(f.get("at") or "undated") for f in failures)))
+    return RECORDER_HEALTHY, (
+        "%d bison watcher(s) beating inside %ss and no recorder failure "
+        "line in that window" % (len(beats), window))
+
+
+
 def main(argv=None):
     p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m src.leadobserve",
                                 description=__doc__)

+class TheHealthReaderAnswersThreeWays(unittest.TestCase):
+    """audit/0002 gap 1: the 14th piece, planted through the REAL sink.
+
+    The reader's whole contract is one sentence - UNHEALTHY MUST NOT READ
+    AS CLEAN - and it is tested in both halves: the states the reader
+    itself answers, and the preflight ask that licenses a PASS on HEALTHY
+    alone. Every plant goes through `watchsink.beat` and `watchsink.record`,
+    the same writers the watcher uses, because a test that wrote its own
+    file shape would only prove the reader can read this test's format.
+    """
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="rga-0002-health-")
+        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.tmp, ignore_errors=True)
+        self.state = os.path.join(self.tmp, "work")
+        os.makedirs(self.state, exist_ok=True)
+        self._queue = os.environ.get("QUEUE")
+        os.environ["QUEUE"] = os.path.join(self.state, "queue.jsonl")
+        self.addCleanup(self._restore)
+
+    def _restore(self):
+        if self._queue is None:
+            os.environ.pop("QUEUE", None)
+        else:
+            os.environ["QUEUE"] = self._queue
+
+    def _ask(self):
+        """The bounce ask, asked exactly as `evaluate` asks it: a record
+        with NO bounce event, so the only thing that can differ between
+        the arms of this class is the recorder's health."""
+        from src import preflight
+        ctx = {"key": "health-1", "email": "someone@example.invalid",
+               "domain": "example.invalid",
+               "record": {"id": "health-1", "events": []}}
+        return preflight._ask_bounce_history(ctx)
+
+    def test_not_running_is_unknown_and_licenses_nothing(self):
+        """No heartbeat at all. NOT RUNNING IS NOT HEALTHY, and the cell
+        stays UNKNOWN - which is what it already said, so the reader only
+        adds the REASON."""
+        health, why = leadobserve.recorder_health()
+        self.assertEqual(leadobserve.RECORDER_UNKNOWN, health)
+        self.assertIn("not running", why)
+        from src import preflight
+        self.assertIsInstance(self._ask(), preflight.Undecided)
+
+    def test_a_fresh_beat_with_no_failures_is_healthy_and_licenses_the_pass(
+            self):
+        """The PASS arm, without which every other arm is satisfied by a
+        reader that answers UNKNOWN to everything. One fresh beat, no
+        failure line: HEALTHY, and the ask returns None - the first
+        legitimate `bounce_history` PASS this instrument has ever been able
+        to print for a contact with no recorded bounce."""
+        watchsink.beat("bison", campaign=487,
+                       state={"status": "active", "leads": 10})
+        health, why = leadobserve.recorder_health()
+        self.assertEqual(leadobserve.RECORDER_HEALTHY, health)
+        self.assertIsNone(self._ask())
+
+    def test_a_failure_line_with_a_fresh_beat_is_failing_never_clean(self):
+        """C2's own trap, closed: the beat is FRESH and the loop is UP,
+        and the recorder is still failing. A health reader that trusted
+        the heartbeat would call this healthy."""
+        watchsink.record(
+            "bison", "%s 487: RuntimeError" % leadobserve.RECORDER_FAILED_KIND,
+            campaign=487)
+        watchsink.beat("bison", campaign=487,
+                       state={"status": "active", "leads": 10})
+        health, why = leadobserve.recorder_health()
+        self.assertEqual(leadobserve.RECORDER_FAILING, health)
+        self.assertIn("failure line", why)
+        from src import preflight
+        self.assertIsInstance(self._ask(), preflight.Undecided)
+
+    def test_a_stale_beat_is_unknown_not_healthy(self):
+        """A watcher that stopped polling. The event log going quiet and
+        the watcher dying look identical from the events alone - the
+        heartbeat's age is what separates them, so stale is UNKNOWN."""
+        stale_at = time.time() - (leadobserve.HEALTH_WINDOW_SECONDS + 600)
+        watchsink.beat("bison", campaign=487, at=stale_at)
+        health, why = leadobserve.recorder_health()
+        self.assertEqual(leadobserve.RECORDER_UNKNOWN, health)
+        self.assertIn("stale", why)
+        from src import preflight
+        self.assertIsInstance(self._ask(), preflight.Undecided)
+
+    def test_a_torn_fragment_of_a_failure_line_still_fails(self):
+        """The half-written line, planted as raw bytes with no newline so

+        path = watchsink.events_path("bison", 487)
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+        with open(path, "ab") as handle:

+        health, why = leadobserve.recorder_health()

+        from src import preflight
+        self.assertIsInstance(self._ask(), preflight.Undecided)
+
+    def test_an_old_failure_outside_the_window_is_not_failing(self):
+        """The window is real, not decoration: a failure older than two
+        bison intervals, with the watcher beating now, is HISTORY rather
+        than the present state - recorded, reported, not a live failure."""
+        old_at = time.time() - (leadobserve.HEALTH_WINDOW_SECONDS + 3600)
+        watchsink.record(
+            "bison", "%s 487: RuntimeError" % leadobserve.RECORDER_FAILED_KIND,
+            campaign=487, at=old_at)
+        watchsink.beat("bison", campaign=487,
+                       state={"status": "active", "leads": 10})
+        health, why = leadobserve.recorder_health()
+        self.assertEqual(leadobserve.RECORDER_HEALTHY, health)
+        self.assertIsNone(self._ask())
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
```

### 1.3 The health reader's spec (deliverable 3)

WHAT IT READS. Two things, both already on disk because the watcher
writes them every poll: the heartbeat (`heartbeat/<watcher>.json`,
rewritten on every poll including the ones that emit nothing, read through
`watchsink.heartbeats()`), and the event log's failure lines
(`watchsink.events` filtered to `RECORDER_FAILED_KIND`, the kind the
writer at `scripts/bison_watch_loop.py`:601 emits). The window is
`HEALTH_WINDOW_SECONDS` - two bison poll intervals - so a failure older
than two intervals is history, and a beat older than two intervals is
stale.

WHAT IT RETURNS. A pair `(state, why)` with exactly three states:

- `RECORDER_HEALTHY` - a fresh beat inside the window, and no failure
  line inside it. `why` says so in words.
- `RECORDER_FAILING` - a failure line inside the window, whatever the
  heartbeat says.
- `RECORDER_UNKNOWN` - no heartbeat at all, or a beat too stale to mean
  anything, or a heartbeat that cannot be read. `why` names which.

WHAT IT RETURNS WHEN THE RECORDER IS UNHEALTHY, AND WHY THAT CANNOT READ
AS CLEAN. Unhealthy is two different facts and both are refused, not
laundered:

- FAILING is the trap the design exists for: the beat is FRESH and the
  loop is UP, and the recorder is still failing. A reader that trusted
  the heartbeat would call this healthy; the failure line outranks the
  beat, and the test plants exactly this arrangement (fresh beat plus
  failure line) and demands FAILING.
- UNKNOWN covers not-running and stale. A torn fragment of a failure
  line - raw bytes with no newline - is dated None, and undated is not
  old, so a fragment carrying the kind is FAILING, not history.
- and the ask is the second half of the contract: the
  `_ask_bounce_history` tail licenses a PASS on HEALTHY alone, so FAILING
  and UNKNOWN both leave the cell UNKNOWN. Unhealthy never reads as clean
  at the reader OR at the cell - mutation C (the ask's health gate
  deleted) reddens four tests, one per unhealthy arm.


### 1.4 Instrument or safety

INSTRUMENT. The reader changes what the system can PROVE about a fact
that is already true or already false - the recorder did or did not fail -
and changes nothing about what the system PERMITS. Before it, a contact
with no recorded bounce was UNKNOWN; after it, that same contact is PASS
when the recorder is healthy and UNKNOWN when it is not. The direction of
every refusal is unchanged: unknown health was already blocking (as
UNKNOWN), and the reader only adds the condition under which the block
lifts. No guard, gate, cap or client config is touched; the ask's existing
EXCLUDED arm is untouched.

The one thing that would have made this a SAFETY change - widening what
`bounce_history` may answer - is deliberately not done: the ask still
returns EXCLUDED for a recorded bounce and Undecided for everything it
cannot see, and the new PASS arm fires only on the health reader's
HEALTHY, which is a fact about the recorder rather than a permission for
the contact.

## 2. Gap 2 - the producer discards the totals the consumer demands

### 2.1 The finding, re-derived

The consumer side already refuses correctly:
`campaignmembership.proven_complete` demands `complete is True` AND
`leads_reported` an int AND `leads_read >= leads_reported` AND the
campaign not named in `incomplete`. A non-match on
`internal_campaign_membership` needs every internal-or-unknown campaign
proven complete, so the rule can EXCLUDE and cannot PASS until the
listing carries those numbers.

The producer throws them away, in TWO places, and the second is not the
one the brief named:

- `scripts/build_collision_index.py`:73 - `page_rows, _total =
  bison._paged(...)`: the provider's own per-campaign total is bound to a
  name and never used.
- `scripts/build_collision_index.py`:95 - `campaigns, _total =
  bison.list_all_campaigns()`: the provider's own LISTING-level total is
  discarded the same way, one level up.
- and `scripts/build_collision_index.py`:113 - the campaign entry written
  into the index records `owner`, `leads_read` and `complete` only, so
  even a `_total` that somebody kept would have nowhere to live.

Both provider functions DO return the total (`bison._paged` and
`bison.list_all_campaigns` both document a `(rows, total)` pair; verified
in the canary tree's `src/providers/bison.py`, which this lane reads and
does not touch). The numbers exist at the call and die at the binding.


### 2.2 Is keeping the provider total at :73 sufficient? NO (deliverable 4)

Keeping the per-walk total at `:73` alone is NOT sufficient, for three
measured reasons:

1. **A kept total that is not RECORDED is still discarded.** The campaign
   entry at `:113` does not carry it. `proven_complete` reads the ENTRY,
   not the call site, so binding `_total` to a real name changes nothing
   until `"leads_reported": <that name>` is written into the entry. The
   proposal records it raw - whatever type the provider returned - and
   the CONSUMER validates the shape (an int, not a bool), because the
   reader cannot verify a number it did not measure, only its presence
   and type; anything else answers PARTIAL, which is the safe direction.
2. **The listing-level total at `:95` is a separate discard.** A listing
   truncated at its own cap is missing WHOLE campaigns. The ask's
   completeness loop can only judge campaigns that HAVE entries;
   `declared_but_not_walked` catches only the operator-declared internal
   ones; an unknown-owner campaign the listing never carried is invisible.
   That is the level ABOVE `proven_complete`, and nothing in the estate
   could see it before the producer kept `campaigns_reported`.
3. **The consumer must refuse on it, or the number is decoration.** A
   total that is recorded and never read is this estate's recurring
   defect (a thing computed correctly that nothing downstream reads). The
   proposal's consumer teeth are `campaignmembership.listing_complete`,
   consulted by the ask, and they are proven by mutation below.

So the answer to deliverable 4 is: keep BOTH totals, RECORD both, and
make the consumer REFUSE on both - which is what the diff below does, and
nothing less.


### 2.3 The smallest change, UNAPPLIED

Three edits and one test file. The producer keeps both totals and
writes them into the index. The consumer gains one function,
`listing_complete`, and the ask consults it ON THE NON-MATCH PATH ONLY -
the placement is load-bearing and is the one thing this audit got wrong
before measuring it:

THE PLACEMENT. The first version of this proposal put the listing-total
refusal in `covers_channel`, which the ask consults BEFORE it looks the
address up. That placement UN-EXCLUDES a member of a DECLARED internal
campaign whose lead row WAS read - a lead row that was read exists
whatever the listing's total says, and the ask's own docstring declares
that asymmetry. The refusal belongs with the other non-match completeness
checks (`proven_complete`, `declared_but_not_walked`), after the lookup.
Mutation E below is the proof that this matters: the same refusal hoisted
back above the lookup reddens exactly the asymmetry test and nothing
else.

### 2.4 Instrument or safety

INSTRUMENT. The rule's semantics do not move: a MATCH is still an
exclusion, a non-match still needs every campaign proven complete, and the
rule still cannot PASS on a listing that cannot prove its own walk. What
changes is that a listing which CAN prove it - because the producer
stopped discarding the proof - is now able to. Before the change, PASS was
unreachable for a true reason the system could not see; after it, PASS is
reachable exactly when the truth supports it, and every refusal that
exists today still fires on every incomplete listing (mutation D: disarm
`listing_complete` and the new refusal test reddens; arm it and the 41
membership tests are green).

The one judgement call that could have made this safety-adjacent -
whether a listing with NO `campaigns_reported` (one written by the old
producer) should be refused - is resolved in the safe direction without
widening anything: such a listing is already refused PER CAMPAIGN (no
entry carries `leads_reported`, so `proven_complete` refuses every
campaign and the non-match is UNKNOWN anyway). The absent key therefore
needs no new refusal, and no existing PASS becomes unreachable.

## 3. Gap 3 - the four hold rules have no input path

### 3.1 The finding, re-derived

The four rows at `src/preflight.py`:942-967 (`hold_active_sequence`,
`hold_recent_touch`, `hold_total_sends`, `cooling_90_days`) all declare
`needs_provider_read: True` and `ask: None`, and `evaluate` short-circuits
on exactly that flag at `src/preflight.py`:1284-1289: the cell is UNKNOWN with
a fixed why, before any ask could run. There is no input path: nothing in
the estate produces a provider-touch truth a rule could read, so the hold
rules answer UNKNOWN for every contact, which is correct and permanent.
`RULES_WITHOUT_DECLARED_AUTHORITY` at `src/preflight.py`:980 lists them -
the declaration itself is the defect, TASK-0190's rule: a rule declaring
no authority may not report PASS.

The `suppression.decide` side already consumes the right shape
(`provider_touches` with `total_sends`, `last_touch_at`,
`active_sequence`) and already fails closed when it is not supplied
(`src/suppression.py`:304-313: "not supplied" appends
`HOLD_TOUCH_HISTORY_UNKNOWN`). What is missing is the AUTHORITY: a file
somebody produces from a read-only provider read, and a reader with the
refusal discipline the other authorities have.


### 3.2 The smallest change, UNAPPLIED

One new module, four asks, and the RULES rows that connect them:

- `src/providertouches.py` (NEW FILE, READ ONLY): reads
  `provider-touches.json` beside the queue (following
  `store.queue_path()`, the same discipline as `campaignmembership`),
  validates the shape, and answers per-LEG coverage: a channel leg is
  covered only when the read says it read it. `lookup` returns the leg's
  row or None - None is NOT COVERED, never "nobody touched". Tri-state
  fields: a null `total_sends` means the read could not see it, and is
  never a zero.
- `src/preflight.py`: a `provider_touches` authority in AUTHORITIES, four
  asks built from one factory (they wrap `suppression.decide`, because
  the row's own `decides` field names that function and a second
  implementation of a hold is how two holds drift), RULES rows that drop
  `needs_provider_read` and declare `needs: ("provider_touches",)`, and
  two new controls (10: a planted active sequence EXCLUDES; 11: a
  fully-seen, nothing-held row PASSES all four cells).
- the tests: seven new arms, the import pin re-pinned with an explicit
  READERS allowlist, and the control count 9 -> 11.

WHERE THE INPUT PATH ATTACHES (deliverable 5). To the authority table,
the same way every other rule's input attaches: the four rows declare
`("provider_touches",)`, the authority gate at the top of `evaluate` runs
before any ask, and an authority that is not there makes the cell UNKNOWN
before the ask is even called. The FILE is produced outside this lane -
`HOW_TO_PRODUCE` says so - by the operator's read-only provider read from
the MAIN checkout, the same arrangement as the collision index.

WHAT THE FOUR RULES RETURN WITH NO PROVIDER DATA: UNKNOWN, never PASS,
and the UNKNOWN is named five different ways so the operator can tell
them apart: the authority is absent or unreadable (the gate);
PRESENT_EMPTY - a valid read that covered nobody; the leg was not read
(HeyReach today); no row for this address on the read leg; a row whose
needed field is null. Each has a test. Each is UNKNOWN at the cell, never
subtracted, never a zero.

THE SEND-PATH HOLE IS PRICED, NOT FIXED HERE. `suppression.decide` reads
a null `active_sequence` as falsy - no hold - at `src/suppression.py`:317.
That is a SAFETY change to close (it alters what the SEND path permits,
not what the preflight can prove), so it is an operator item: the ASK does
not lean on the decider for the null-check and does its own per-field
tri-state check instead, and the decider is left untouched.

```diff
diff --git a/g3_providertouches_new.py b/g3_providertouches_new.py
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..473a41216
--- /dev/null
+++ b/g3_providertouches_new.py
@@ -0,0 +1,171 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""What the providers say they already did to this person. READ ONLY.
+
+## THE FOUR ROWS THIS EXISTS TO FEED
+
+`hold_active_sequence`, `hold_recent_touch`, `hold_total_sends` and
+`cooling_90_days` in the preflight ask what the PROVIDERS know, whoever
+sent it. `suppression.decide` takes `provider_touches` as an argument for
+exactly that reason - the record's event log knows only touches THIS
+SYSTEM made, and the holds are about the person, not about us - and until
+this module existed no preflight rule could supply the argument, so those
+four rules were UNKNOWN by construction and a landed provider read cleared
+nothing.
+
+## THE AUTHORITY, AND WHO PRODUCES IT
+
+One operator read, per cohort, per channel, read-only:
+
+    email     the eligib/0001 paste (GET-only EmailBison) and its parser
+    linkedin  the HeyReach reads, which are POST-only - an operator
+              decision recorded in eligib/0002, not a thing this module
+              assumes
+
+It lands beside the queue, gitignored, like every other file of real
+people. Nothing in this module makes a provider call, and nothing in it
+writes the file; `HOW_TO_PRODUCE` below is the whole of its opinion on
+how it comes to exist.
+
+The shape this module requires of it:
+
+    {
+     "generated_at": "<ISO-8601 UTC>",
+     "channels": {"email": {"read": true, "why": "<...>"},
+                  "linkedin": {"read": false, "why": "<...>"}},
+     "by_email": {"<address>": {
+         "email":    {"last_touch_at": <iso>|null,
+                      "total_sends": <int>|null,
+                      "active_sequence": <bool>|null},
+         "linkedin": {<same three keys, or the leg is absent>}}}}
+
+EVERY FIELD IS TRI-STATE. `null` means THE READ COULD NOT SEE IT, never
+"none of them": a send count the read could not produce is UNKNOWN, not
+zero, and this module never converts one into the other in either
+direction. A contact with no row at all was not covered by the read. A
+channel with `"read": false` was not read. Every one of those is UNKNOWN
+downstream - `suppression.decide` itself answers HOLD when its
+`provider_touches` argument is absent, which is the send-path shape of the
+same rule, and the preflight shape is the cell reading UNKNOWN.
+"""
+import json
+import os
+
+from . import store
+
+
+class TouchUnreadable(Exception):
+    """The provider-touch authority is absent, unparseable or malformed.
+
+    IT RAISES, for the same reason `campaignmembership.MembershipUnreadable`
+    does: this reader has no send-path caller and exists to answer a
+    preflight question, where "I could not look" and "nobody was touched"
+    must never be the same answer.
+    """
+
+
+#: The one honest sentence about production, and it is not this lane's to run.
+HOW_TO_PRODUCE = (
+    "run the operator's read-only provider read from the MAIN checkout - "
+    "the eligib/0001 paste for the EmailBison leg, the HeyReach leg per the "
+    "operator's own POST decision - and let its parser write "
+    "provider-touches.json beside the queue")
+
+
+#: Every key this module requires. A file missing any one of them is
+#: UNREADABLE rather than empty: a read that says nothing about which
+#: channels it covered is not a read of both.
+REQUIRED_KEYS = {
+    "generated_at": "the read's own timestamp - a read with no time cannot "
+                    "be judged fresh or stale",
+    "channels": "which legs the read covered - the per-channel question "
+                "cannot be routed without it",
+    "by_email": "the per-contact touch rows themselves",
+}
+
+
+def path():
+    """The authority's absolute path. Resolved per call, never cached.
+
+    Beside the queue rather than beside the repository, the same discipline
+    `campaignmembership.path()` uses and for the same reasons: it is real
+    people, it is gitignored, and it moves when `store.use_directory` moves
+    the rest of the state. No environment override of its own - following
+    `queue_path()` is what makes it move for free.
+    """
+    return os.path.abspath(
+        os.path.join(os.path.dirname(store.queue_path()),
+                     "provider-touches.json"))
+
+
+def load(file_path=None):
+    """The authority, validated. RAISES rather than answering emptily."""
+    file_path = file_path or path()
+    if not os.path.exists(file_path):
+        raise TouchUnreadable(
+            "%s does not exist. What the providers have already done to "
+            "these people is the only input the four hold/cooling rules "
+            "have, and an absent read is not a read of nobody: %s"
+            % (file_path, HOW_TO_PRODUCE))
+    try:
+        with open(file_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            index = json.load(handle)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        raise TouchUnreadable(
+            "%s could not be read (%s: %s)"
+            % (file_path, type(exc).__name__, str(exc)[:160])) from None
+    if not isinstance(index, dict):
+        raise TouchUnreadable(
+            "%s does not hold an object at its top level" % (file_path,))
+    missing = sorted(k for k in REQUIRED_KEYS if k not in index)
+    if missing:
+        raise TouchUnreadable(
+            "%s is missing %s. %s"
+            % (file_path, ", ".join("`%s` (%s)" % (k, REQUIRED_KEYS[k])
+                                    for k in missing), HOW_TO_PRODUCE))
+    for key in ("channels", "by_email"):
+        if not isinstance(index[key], dict):
+            raise TouchUnreadable(
+                "%s: `%s` is not an object" % (file_path, key))
+    return index
+
+
+def records(index):
+    """How many contact rows the read holds. The authority's own count."""
+    return len(index.get("by_email") or {})
+
+
+def covers_channel(index, channel):
+    """(bool, why). Did this read cover the channel being asked about?
+
+    A channel leg that is `{"read": false}` or absent was NOT read, and a
+    missing leg is reported rather than assumed: whether an email-only
+    canary may clear a `channel: "both"` rule on its email leg alone is the
+    operator's scoping decision (eligib/0002 recorded all three options),
+    not a default this module picks.
+    """
+    leg = (index.get("channels") or {}).get(channel)
+    if isinstance(leg, dict) and leg.get("read") is True:
+        return True, "the %s leg of the read at %s" % (
+            channel, index.get("generated_at"))
+    why = (leg.get("why") if isinstance(leg, dict) else None)
+    return False, ("the read did not cover the %s leg (%s), so no %s "
+                   "provider truth can be ruled out"
+                   % (channel, why or "no leg recorded at all", channel))
+
+
+def lookup(index, email=None, channel=None):
+    """The `provider_touches` dict for one address and one channel.
+
+    Returns the leg's dict, or None. None means NOT COVERED - no row for
+    this address, or no leg for this channel - and the caller must treat
+    it as UNKNOWN, never as an empty touch history: a person the read did
+    not see is not a person nobody touched.
+    """
+    address = (email or "").strip().lower()
+    row = (index.get("by_email") or {}).get(address)
+    if not isinstance(row, dict):
+        return None
+    leg = row.get(channel)
+    if not isinstance(leg, dict):
+        return None
+    return leg
```

### 3.3 Instrument or safety

INSTRUMENT for the input path and the asks. The four rules'
semantics are the rows' own `decides` fields, delegated to the one
function that already owns them; nothing the system PERMITS changes,
because preflight is a proof instrument and not the send path. Every new
arm refuses in the safe direction, and the unsafe readings - an uncovered
leg reading as covered, an absent row reading as zero sends - are the two
mutations that reddened:

- mutation A - `covers_channel` lying that an unread leg is covered -
  reddened 4 tests;
- mutation B - `lookup` answering an empty dict for a person the read
  never saw - reddened 3 tests, but only AFTER the leg test's assertion
  was strengthened from "linkedin in why" to the exact refusal phrase,
  because two different UNKNOWNs shared the weaker assertion. The
  strengthening is itself part of the finding: a mutation that survives a
  test is not a proof, and the test was fixed to name which UNKNOWN it
  means.

The one safety-relevant decision inside the design - the send-path
`active_sequence` hole above - is deliberately NOT closed by this
proposal, because closing it in `suppression.decide` would change what
the send path permits, and that is the operator's call with a price tag
in section 5.


### 3.4 Verification

The composed tree is the canary tip's tree plus the three gap-3 files
(1348 files). Against it, this session re-ran:

- `Ran 53 tests in 3.095s - OK`

The instrument can print the other answer, which is the whole deliverable
for a rule that only ever refused: control 11 is a fully-seen row with
nothing held, and all four cells read PASS; control 10 is the same world
with one planted active sequence, and the cell reads EXCLUDED with the
hold named in the why. Controls 10 and 11 differ in exactly one field,
which is the control discipline this module already carries.

Mutations A and B above were applied to this same tree, reddened their
named tests, and were restored by byte-identical copy; the quoted run is
post-restore.


## 4. The honest total (deliverable 6)

With the 13 asks (audit/0001), the 4 hold asks and the 1 health reader
all built and landed, what does 23/23 require? The honest answer is that
13+4+1 removes every CODE-side blocker and leaves every HANDS-side one,
plus one scoping decision that is not this lane's to make:

- what 13+4+1 BUYS: every one of the 23 rules can now print every answer
  on the email leg - PASS, EXCLUDED, or an UNKNOWN that names its cause.
  The three structural refusals are closed: `bounce_history` can PASS
  (recorder healthy), `internal_campaign_membership` can PASS (a listing
  that kept its totals), and the four hold rules can PASS or EXCLUDE (a
  provider-touch read that covered the contact).
- what still stands between 13+4+1 and 23/23, in order of whose hands:
  1. the operator's READS, from the main checkout, read-only: rerun
     `build_collision_index.py` (gap 2's producer change makes the new
     listing carry its totals), produce `provider-touches.json`, and have
     the bison watcher running so the health reader has a heartbeat to
     read. None of these is code; all of them are the operator's.
  2. the SCOPING DECISION: the four hold rows are `channel: "both"`, and
     the linkedin leg has no read (HeyReach is behind the operator's
     acceptance decision). An email-leg PASS on `hold_total_sends`
     asserts the EMAIL total is under threshold - the linkedin sends are
     unmeasured. Whether an email-scoped canary may treat the email leg
     as the whole answer is eligib/0002's question, not this audit's; it
     is priced below. Without the decision, a both-channel assessment
     keeps those cells UNKNOWN - correctly.
  3. HeyReach POST acceptance (the linkedin leg's read, behind an
     operator decision) and the 18 profileUrl sourcings audit/0001
     already priced, for the rules that need them.

So: 23/23 IS reachable - on an email-scoped reading, with the reads done
and the scoping decision taken - and it is NOT reachable by code alone,
and NOT reachable on a both-channel reading while HeyReach stays
unread. The earliest honest date is **Monday 2026-10-20, end of day**:
the operator's own hands are the constraint (the reads are daywork, not
an overnight build), and Monday is the first working day after this
audit lands Saturday 2026-10-18. That date holds only if the scoping
decision is taken Monday morning and every data precondition resolves
favorably - a read that comes back partial, or a watcher that will not
beat, moves it honestly to the right.


## 5. The operator block

| gap | instrument or safety | cost |
|---|---|---|
| 1 - bounce-recorder health reader (`leadobserve.recorder_health`, one gate in the ask tail) | instrument | one ~40-line reader + one condition + six tests, all written and verified UNAPPLIED in section 1; the operator's share is restarting the bison watcher from the main checkout so there is a heartbeat to read - read-only, no provider write |
| 2 - the listing totals (`build_collision_index` keeps both provider totals; `campaignmembership.listing_complete`; one ask call) | instrument | three producer edits + one consumer function + one ask call + four tests, all verified UNAPPLIED in section 2; the operator's share is one rerun of `build_collision_index.py` from the main checkout - a full read-only walk, the same cost as any previous build |
| 3 - the hold rules' input path (`src/providertouches.py`, four asks wrapping `suppression.decide`, controls 10-11) | instrument | one 171-line READ-ONLY reader module + one ask factory + seven tests, verified UNAPPLIED in section 3; the operator's share is producing `provider-touches.json` (read-only provider read, main checkout) and taking the email-only scoping decision |

Priced and left, because they change what the system PERMITS or spend
what only the operator may spend:

- the `suppression.decide` `active_sequence` null-as-falsy hole
  (`src/suppression.py`:317) - SAFETY, send-path; the ask pre-checks its
  own field so the preflight is not affected, but the SEND path still
  holds nobody for an unseen active sequence;
- HeyReach POST acceptance - the linkedin leg's read;
- the 18 profileUrl sourcings audit/0001 priced;
- the email-only scoping decision (eligib/0002).

**Earliest honest date for 23/23: Monday 2026-10-20, end of day.** Three
rows above, all instrument; every code change is already written, diffed
and verified unapplied; the remaining critical path is the operator's own
hands.
